note: Bremer County Conservation park of 42 acres on the west side of Frederika, on both sides of the Wapsipinicon River at a low-head dam. Over fifty electric sites, not numbered, in an open grassy strip along the gravel road down the park's west edge, ending in a loop by a dock on an arm of the river pool. Two shelters, a boat ramp and canoe access. --Claude
summary: Rates ($20 electric / $15 non-electric), 20/30/50 amp, FCFS and facilities confirmed on the county's mycountyparks page. Stored pin is 520 m off, at a rural road corner; corrected. Waterfront upgrade lead (riverview) from the north loop. Season unsourced.
flags: PIN (lead): the stored 42.880278,-92.317389 is a gravel-road intersection in farm fields about 520 m southwest of the campground. The camping area, the open strip with electric pedestals along the park's west road and the turnaround loop at its north end (the park map's 'Electric Camping' symbol), is centred at about 42.8830,-92.3122 (NAIP). Google's 'Alcock Park - East entrance' at 42.88185,-92.30934 is the day-use side across the river.

WATERFRONT upgrade lead (not waterfront -> riverview proposed): the stored evidence was a cloud-covered satellite read at the wrong pin, so it isn't evidence. At the loop at the north end of the camping strip, open lawn runs about 10-25 m from the loop road to the bank of a west arm of the Wapsipinicon pool above the dam, where the county map shows a dock. That arm is about 55 m wide and opens into a pool about 200 m across, so it is a river, not a creek. The electric pedestals I can see sit on the west side of the camp road, so the road lies between the pads and the water. That rules out on-water, but there's a clear look across the lawn to open water from the north end. No official site photos exist, since sites aren't numbered. The sites further south along the strip look east into woods, with the river channel behind them.
